text:
Sampled evaluation can reverse model rankings relative to full-catalog evaluation. A direct sequential-recommendation study found inconsistencies with both uniform and popularity-weighted samples, including commonly used 100-item candidate sets ([Dallmann et al., 2021](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.13045)). RecSys 2025 examined sampling fidelity, robustness and predictive power, reinforcing that candidate selection affects conclusions ([On the Reliability of Sampling Strategies](https://doi.org/10.1145/3705328.3748086)). Separately, a 2024 sequential-recommendation study comparing training samplers found aggregate accuracy concealed head/mid/tail disparities; random sampling favored head items, while popularity-based methods traded overall performance for more balanced results ([Prakash et al., 2024](https://arxiv.org/abs/2410.17276)). Popularity-weighted sampling is therefore a useful stress test, without guaranteeing agreement with full-catalog rankings.

Practical synthesis: replace raw score-margin probes with a separate training-history ranking audit. Use observed prefix→next-item examples; exclude prefix-seen items while retaining the target. Compare target rank and HR@10 across repeated unique uniform negatives, negatives matched to the target’s training-frequency band, model-scored hard negatives, and the complete eligible catalog. Report target-rank percentiles, hit/miss disagreement, and model-order disagreement across protocols; stratify by history length and target popularity. Bootstrap users with paired resampling across protocols, retaining all examples from each user together; report candidate-resampling variability separately. These are proposed diagnostics, not established findings from the cited papers. Training-history results measure fitted behavior and sensitivity, not generalization; with only twenty audited users, subgroup uncertainty will be substantial. Keep full-catalog unseen-item recommendation lists separate from retrospective target-ranking probes, and preserve pinned four-category macro validation HR@10 as the selection criterion.
